entity_types.definition: A general idea, theoretical construct, or object of study that isn't itself an algorithm, structure, pattern, or technology.
A defined step-by-step procedure for solving a computational problem.
A concrete way of organizing and storing data.
A reusable, named solution to a recurring software design problem.
A high-level architectural approach for structuring a software system.
A named tool, platform, language, database, or framework.
A guiding rule or best practice for design or engineering decisions.
A practical method or approach applied to accomplish a task (distinct from a formal Algorithm).
A measurable quantity used to evaluate a system, algorithm, or process.
A non-functional property a system is designed or evaluated against.
A named individual referenced as an author, practitioner, or figure.
A referenced book, paper, or publication.
A named discipline or area of study.
A named chart type or method for visually representing data.

relation_types.definition: Subject is a kind or subtype of the object.
relation_types.example: DataStructure IS_A Concept (a hash table is a kind of associative container)

relation_types.definition: Subject is a component or member of the object.
relation_types.example: Method PART_OF Algorithm (partitioning is part of quicksort)

relation_types.definition: Subject employs or relies on the object as a building block.
relation_types.example: Algorithm USES DataStructure (Dijkstra's algorithm uses a priority queue)

relation_types.definition: Subject provides a concrete realization of the object.
relation_types.example: DataStructure IMPLEMENTS Concept (a hash table implements a map)

relation_types.definition: Subject addresses or resolves the object (a problem or need).
relation_types.example: Algorithm SOLVES Concept (Dijkstra's algorithm solves shortest-path)

relation_types.definition: Subject enhances or optimizes the object.
relation_types.example: Technique IMPROVES QualityAttribute (indexing improves query performance)

relation_types.definition: Subject is a substitutable option in place of the object.
relation_types.example: ArchitectureStyle ALTERNATIVE_TO ArchitectureStyle (microservices alternative to monolith)

relation_types.definition: Subject is compared against the object to highlight a tradeoff or difference.
relation_types.example: ArchitectureStyle CONTRASTS_WITH ArchitectureStyle (event-driven contrasts with layered)

relation_types.definition: Subject requires the object to function or hold.
relation_types.example: Algorithm DEPENDS_ON DataStructure (heapsort depends on a heap)

relation_types.definition: Subject is a concrete instance illustrating the object.
relation_types.example: Technology EXAMPLE_OF ArchitectureStyle (Kafka is an example of event-driven architecture)

relation_types.definition: Subject formally specifies the meaning of the object.
relation_types.example: Work DEFINES Concept (Design Patterns defines the strategy pattern)

relation_types.definition: Subject is quantified or evaluated using the object.
relation_types.example: QualityAttribute MEASURED_BY Metric (reliability measured by software reliability model)

relation_types.definition: Subject is relevant or applicable within the domain of the object.
relation_types.example: Technique APPLIES_TO Field (exploratory data analysis applies to data science)

relation_types.definition: Subject (a Work) was written by the object (a Person).
relation_types.example: Work AUTHORED_BY Person (Clean Code authored by Robert Martin)

relation_types.definition: Catch-all association when no more specific relation applies.
